text: Besides repeating a key word, a person with a pencil can skip a letter now and then, use each twice, go back and forth, jump by growing steps, or restart at each carved line; or use a row of the sculpture's table as the key ('layer two'). The list was written first.
Each rule groups the known places by the key letter they use; each group must share a key value, on the sculpture's tables or on alphabets in any order.

The run hit its 30-minute budget inside the skip rule, so most of the list went untested here. One cell (skip, two free alphabets) was above ten coppers; 0127 replicated it and 0128 finished the list.
